newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil softens with West.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil softens with West.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps on Monday afternoon extended earlier day losses in line with the weaker IPE but were expected to be supported by physical buying towards the market close, traders said.
"It is coming off a little bit now," a trader said on the gas oil swaps. "IPE is showing some weakness on the gas oil and crude and there is a bit more selling interest."
May gas oil swaps were last traded at $25.62 and $25.66 per barrel, compared to trades in the late morning at $25.70.
Brokers last quoted May swaps at $25.60/$25.65, down from midday's $25.60/$25.75 and Friday's $25.80/$25.90.
June gas oil on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) opened weaker on Monday. At 0555 GMT June was off 50 cents per tonne at $165.50.
In Singapore, the May/June backwardated spread was wide, quoted at $1.00/$1.10 per barrel and was expected to deter further aribtrage exports from the West, traders said.
A trader said he expected local buying interest to re-emerge in the physical market later and repeat Friday's buying of two gas oil and one jet cargo.
On Friday, the traders who have been responsible for the purchase of over 15 million barrels on the Singapore market since March 3 bought two cargoes.

The two 150,000-barrel cargoes traded at $26.70 and $26.30 per barrel for May loading on a free-on-board basis, suggesting that the traders were not expected to pull out of the spot market at least until end April.
The May gas oil/jet fuel (regrade) was last heard only offered at -65 cents per barrel (in favour of gas oil) while June was offered at +60 cents.
Fuel oil swaps were steady from Friday's $97.75/$98.25 quotes for June, brokers said.
